cues.text: Welcome in.
This guided practice is private to your training attempt.
You can pause, replay, or mute me at
any time — and every spoken instruction stays visible on
screen.
As Scribe, you'll turn the team's discussion into a
clear, complete record — then hand it to the
Facilitator.
Your job is simple:
capture Blue decisions accurately, check every required field,
and pass the record to the Facilitator.
Start with Strategic Orientation — the team's north star.
This fixture uses the current choices and the exact narrative
fields Blue needs.

workflow, so what you practice here will feel familiar
later.

As Facilitator, you'll check the team record, coordinate
support, and own the final handoff — to White
Cell.
Review the team record, use the support workspaces,
and submit only when the artifact is genuinely ready.
Each workspace answers one question:
what changed, what should we project, what should
we ask, what should we message, and what
needs attention now?
A forwarded artifact is ready for your review — not
automatically ready for White Cell.
An R F I — a Request for Information —
asks White Cell for a ruling, clarification, or
scenario detail.
When you revise it, keep the same record.
Keep the channels straight.
Answers stay with the R F I, direct messages
live in Communications, and alerts point you to the
right record.
Before you finish, recall the role boundary:
who reviews, communicates, projects, and makes the
final submission?
Use lifecycle and timeline evidence to verify submission.
Projection — or one button press — does not prove
it landed.

As Notetaker, you'll capture how the team reached a
decision — while keeping your notes separate from official artifacts
Your notes preserve the why behind a decision.
They do not author, approve, or submit the
team's action.
Context makes a note useful later.
Capture when the reasoning happened — and which decision it
informed.
Use the right kind of evidence:
an observation explains reasoning, a key moment marks a
turn, and a quote preserves exact words.
Your move notes belong to your Notetaker seat.
A manual save can publish a structured timeline snapshot —
without replacing another seat's work.
This inject changes the scenario.
Capture how the team interprets it — but do not
edit the official action.
Choose the Notetaker record for the explanation.
Then confirm that the official timeline stays read-only.
Finish with the ownership map:
what stays with your seat, what is shared,
and which official surfaces stay read-only.
